title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after a traffic stop on July 23. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister when a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, reading the final digit as 7 instead of 2, and flagged the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate police cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another vehicle.

The sisters filed lawsuits on January 3 seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was wrongly stopped in April after being mistaken for an armed robbery suspect and forced to kneel with his hands on his head. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits will now proceed in state District Court.
